questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Matrix Product Using the Distributive Law
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13995865/assets/c1d9f53c6aed4acd378f8554df5c8beaaea81e169b5284e51f87204a87b3d53d.png)

A housing complex designed by an architect is shown in the coordinate plane as the region $R$ with vertices $ABCD.$ A highway lies on the line $l$ with equation $2x+y+1=0.$ The area of the complex is $16$ hectares.

Current part:

$$
X+Y=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\,Z=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Knowing that the matrix representation $T=[\begin{aligned}{t}_{11} & {t}_{12} \\ {t}_{21} & {t}_{22}\end{aligned}]$ of a linear transformation $T$ is given by

$$
T=XZ+YZ,
$$

find the values ${t}_{ij}.$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${t}_{11}=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        
$\,{t}_{12}=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-2}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                                

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${t}_{21}=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-3}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        
$\,{t}_{22}=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-4}}
questions.worked_solution:
We apply the distributive law

$$
XZ+YZ=(X+Y)Z.
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =XZ+YZ \\  & =(X+Y)Z \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $R$ (the old housing complex) and the area of the image $T(R)$ (the new housing complex) under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(R))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(R)
$$

We're given that

$$
\text{Area}(R)=16\,\text{hectares}.
$$

Computing the determinant of the matrix $T$ (found in part 1), we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-3)\cdot (-1)-(2)\cdot 0 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(R)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(R) \\  & =3\cdot 16 \\  & =48.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the new housing complex is $48$ hectares.

questions.worked_solution:
In part 1, we found that the matrix representation of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of the larger recreational area:

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of the smaller recreational area, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-1)(-3)-0}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}15 & 15 & 21 \\ 18 & 24 & 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 & 7 \\ 6 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the vertices of the smaller recreational area are $L(5,6),$ $M(5,8),$ and $N(7,8).$

questions.worked_solution:
In part 1, we found that the matrix representation of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that the line $2x+y+1=0$ passes through the points $U(-1,1)$ and $V(0,-1)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $U$ and $V$ under the action of $T,$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${U}^{′}(3,-3)$ and ${V}^{′}(0,1).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${U}^{′}$ and ${V}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-3) & =\frac{1-(-3)}{0-3}(x-3) \\ y+3 & =-\frac{4}{3}(x-3) \\ 3y+9 & =-4x+12 \\ 4x+3y+9 & =12 \\ 4x+3y & =3\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot 3-4\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the solution to this system as

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
